- [relevant] Fact: 轉交事實一
  Alex's own words: 原話
  Matching to-do: (none given)
  The assistant's reasoning: 理由
  (2026-10-26T10:00)

How to handle them (these handoffs in themselves count as a substantive change):
- [resolves]: Alex has already dealt with or answered the matching to-do. Remove that item from
  `## 待辦` (match by meaning; the wording may differ), and write the fact into the right section of STATE.md.
- [changes]: the matching to-do still stands, but its premise or date has changed. Rewrite that item according to the
  fact, and update related sections if needed.
- [relevant]: for reference only; update STATE.md only if it affects the current state.
- [answers]: Alex answered a question this project asked (matching to-do = the original question, fact = the
  answer). Write the decision into the related sections; a to-do waiting on this answer is removed or rewritten
  according to it.
- If the matching to-do cannot be found in STATE.md, do not force the fact onto another item; only record it in the
  related section (if it is relevant).
- The "fact" is the assistant's retelling and may sound more certain than what Alex actually said. Where there is a
  quote, the quote wins; when writing into STATE.md keep the uncertain tone (expected, planned, might, intends to) rather
  than stating it as settled.


For background, read ./AGENT.md and ./STATE.md. **STATE.md is at the project root (./STATE.md), not under memory/**;
there is no STATE.md under memory/, and there must not be one.

How memory/ is organised:
- memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, memory/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md: the raw running record, only ever appended to.
- memory/reference/<topic>.md (README.md is the index): curated topic documents that get rewritten; their content is
  the most accurate current version, and where it conflicts with the older running record, reference/ wins.

Rules:
- Write in English: everything you add to STATE.md (prose and to-do items), and the summary and reason in
  your answer, are in that language, in the style of the text already there. Code, paths, commands and names stay as
  they are.
- Edit STATE.md only when there is a *substantive change* (it is a distilled current state, not a log); with no
  substantive change, do not touch STATE.md at all.
  If STATE.md still holds the placeholder content from onboarding while memory/ already has substantive content, that
  in itself counts as a substantive change.
- Where STATE.md mentions files that have been moved, or open questions that newer content has answered or overturned,
  fix those too.
- STATE.md must have a `## 待辦` section in a fixed format, one item per line:
  `- [ ] 〔Alex〕…` (only Alex can do it: accounts, passwords, payments, a decision or an answer that is
  Alex's to give)
  `- [ ] 〔agent〕…` (an agent can do it directly)
  `- [ ] 〔待定〕…` (blocked until something still open is settled, other than a decision that is Alex's: an
  item waiting on Alex's decision is 〔Alex〕)
  The `(等 Alex:task-…)` at the end of a 〔Alex〕 line is the key of Hugin's task registry: **keep it exactly as
  it is, and do not change that line's text** (when Hugin closes the task, Alex's line is removed
  automatically by its key; if the text changes, the key no longer matches).
  With no to-dos, write `- (無)`. List only what is not yet done and concretely actionable; remove what is done,
  overturned or out of date instead of leaving it ticked. To-dos go only in this section: do not open other lists such
  as "next steps" or "not done yet" anywhere else in STATE.md.
- Do not create, modify or delete any file other than ./STATE.md.

  Alex's to give)

The format of the edit list:
- edits are {"old", "new"} pairs applied in order: old must be a passage of the **current STATE.md that occurs exactly
  once** (verbatim, newlines included; if it is so short that it occurs several times, take a few more characters), and
  new is the text that replaces it (an empty string deletes the passage). Do not return the whole STATE.md.
- With nothing to change: state_updated: false, edits: [].
- The `(等 Alex:task-…)` marker at the end of a 〔Alex〕 line must not change; when that item is done, delete the
  whole line.
- summary and reason are written in English, like the text in STATE.md.

  the project's own wording; match by meaning. If it affects that to-do, rewrite it according to the fact; otherwise
  record it in the related section. A note does not mean the work is done: do not delete a to-do because of a note.
- [dismissed]: Alex decided this question needs no answer. Remove the to-do waiting on the answer; record why if
  that is useful.
- [same_as]: Hugin merged this item with the same one in another project; for reference only, the to-dos stay
  as they are.
- "The assistant's reasoning" says who decided and on what grounds: if Alex decided, write it that way; if
  Hugin concluded it from evidence, mark it in STATE.md as an inference, and do not write it as something
  Alex said.

  the project's own wording; match by meaning. If it affects that to-do, rewrite it according to the fact; otherwise

- [dismissed]: Alex decided this question needs no answer. Remove the to-do waiting on the answer; record why if
  that is useful.
- [same_as]: Hugin merged this item with the same one in another project; for reference only, the to-dos stay
  as they are.
- "The assistant's reasoning" says who decided and on what grounds: if Alex decided, write it that way; if
  Hugin concluded it from evidence, mark it in STATE.md as an inference, and do not write it as something
  Alex said.

## 待辦
- [ ] 〔agent〕做一件事

STATE>>>

Rules:
- Write in English: everything you add to STATE.md (prose and to-do items), and the summary and reason in
  your answer, are in that language, in the style of the text already there. Code, paths, commands and names stay as
  they are.
- Edit STATE.md only when there is a *substantive change* (it is a distilled current state, not a log); with no
  substantive change, do not touch STATE.md at all.
  If STATE.md still holds the placeholder content from onboarding while memory/ already has substantive content, that
  in itself counts as a substantive change.
- Where STATE.md mentions files that have been moved, or open questions that newer content has answered or overturned,
  fix those too.
- STATE.md must have a `## 待辦` section in a fixed format, one item per line:
  `- [ ] 〔Alex〕…` (only Alex can do it: accounts, passwords, payments, a decision or an answer that is
  Alex's to give)
  `- [ ] 〔agent〕…` (an agent can do it directly)
  `- [ ] 〔待定〕…` (blocked until something still open is settled, other than a decision that is Alex's: an
  item waiting on Alex's decision is 〔Alex〕)
  The `(等 Alex:task-…)` at the end of a 〔Alex〕 line is the key of Hugin's task registry: **keep it exactly as
  it is, and do not change that line's text** (when Hugin closes the task, Alex's line is removed
  automatically by its key; if the text changes, the key no longer matches).
  With no to-dos, write `- (無)`. List only what is not yet done and concretely actionable; remove what is done,
  overturned or out of date instead of leaving it ticked. To-dos go only in this section: do not open other lists such
  as "next steps" or "not done yet" anywhere else in STATE.md.

The format of the edit list:
- edits are {"old", "new"} pairs applied in order: old must be a passage of the **current STATE.md that occurs exactly
  once** (verbatim, newlines included; if it is so short that it occurs several times, take a few more characters), and
  new is the text that replaces it (an empty string deletes the passage). Do not return the whole STATE.md.
- With nothing to change: state_updated: false, edits: [].
- The `(等 Alex:task-…)` marker at the end of a 〔Alex〕 line must not change; when that item is done, delete the
  whole line.
- summary and reason are written in English, like the text in STATE.md.

there is no STATE.md under memory/, and there must not be one.

How memory/ is organised:
- memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, memory/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md: the raw running record, only ever appended to.
- memory/reference/<topic>.md (README.md is the index): curated topic documents that get rewritten; their content is
  the most accurate current version, and where it conflicts with the older running record, reference/ wins.

=== prompt librarian-todo-format @ pdang
Fix only the format of the `## 待辦` section of ./STATE.md. Do not change anything else, nor the content of the
to-dos, and do not touch any other file.

The correct format (one item per line; with no to-dos write `- (無)`; STATE.md must have this section):
  `- [ ] 〔Alex〕…` (only Alex can do it: accounts, passwords, payments, a decision or an answer that is
  Alex's to give, things Alex has to buy or do personally)
  `- [ ] 〔agent〕…` (an agent can do it directly)
  `- [ ] 〔待定〕…` (blocked until something still open is settled, other than a decision that is Alex's: an
  item waiting on Alex's decision is 〔Alex〕)

If STATE.md has to-do-like lists elsewhere (for example "open questions", "needs Alex to decide", "can be done by
an agent", "next steps", "not done yet"), **move** those items into `## 待辦` (marking who is responsible) and
delete the original section; write `- (無)` only when the whole STATE.md truly has no to-dos. Schedules and facts
about finished work are not to-dos: leave them where they are. Anything you write is in English, like the
rest of the file.

The current problems:
STATE.md: a to-do without an owner tag, or a finished one not removed: `- [ ] 沒標負責人的一件事`

Rules:
- Write in English: everything you add to STATE.md (prose and to-do items), and the summary and reason in
  your answer, are in that language, in the style of the text already there. Code, paths, commands and names stay as
  they are.
- Edit STATE.md only when there is a *substantive change* (it is a distilled current state, not a log); with no
  substantive change, do not touch STATE.md at all.
  If STATE.md still holds the placeholder content from onboarding while memory/ already has substantive content, that
  in itself counts as a substantive change.
- Where STATE.md mentions files that have been moved, or open questions that newer content has answered or overturned,
  fix those too.
- STATE.md must have a `## 待辦` section in a fixed format, one item per line:
  `- [ ] 〔Alex〕…` (only Alex can do it: accounts, passwords, payments, a decision or an answer that is
  Alex's to give)
  `- [ ] 〔agent〕…` (an agent can do it directly)
  `- [ ] 〔待定〕…` (blocked until something still open is settled, other than a decision that is Alex's: an
  item waiting on Alex's decision is 〔Alex〕)
  The `(等 Alex:task-…)` at the end of a 〔Alex〕 line is the key of Hugin's task registry: **keep it exactly as
  it is, and do not change that line's text** (when Hugin closes the task, Alex's line is removed
  automatically by its key; if the text changes, the key no longer matches).
  With no to-dos, write `- (無)`. List only what is not yet done and concretely actionable; remove what is done,
  overturned or out of date instead of leaving it ticked. To-dos go only in this section: do not open other lists such
  as "next steps" or "not done yet" anywhere else in STATE.md.

The format of the edit list:
- edits are {"old", "new"} pairs applied in order: old must be a passage of the **current STATE.md that occurs exactly
  once** (verbatim, newlines included; if it is so short that it occurs several times, take a few more characters), and
  new is the text that replaces it (an empty string deletes the passage). Do not return the whole STATE.md.
- With nothing to change: state_updated: false, edits: [].
- The `(等 Alex:task-…)` marker at the end of a 〔Alex〕 line must not change; when that item is done, delete the
  whole line.
- summary and reason are written in English, like the text in STATE.md.

How to handle them (these handoffs in themselves count as a substantive change):
- [resolves]: Alex has already dealt with or answered the matching to-do. Remove that item from
  `## 待辦` (match by meaning; the wording may differ), and write the fact into the right section of STATE.md.
- [changes]: the matching to-do still stands, but its premise or date has changed. Rewrite that item according to the
  fact, and update related sections if needed.
- [relevant]: for reference only; update STATE.md only if it affects the current state.
- [answers]: Alex answered a question this project asked (matching to-do = the original question, fact = the
  answer). Write the decision into the related sections; a to-do waiting on this answer is removed or rewritten
  according to it.
- If the matching to-do cannot be found in STATE.md, do not force the fact onto another item; only record it in the
  related section (if it is relevant).
- The "fact" is the assistant's retelling and may sound more certain than what Alex actually said. Where there is a
  quote, the quote wins; when writing into STATE.md keep the uncertain tone (expected, planned, might, intends to) rather
  than stating it as settled.


For background, read ./AGENT.md and ./STATE.md. **STATE.md is at the project root (./STATE.md), not under memory/**;
there is no STATE.md under memory/, and there must not be one.

How memory/ is organised:
- memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, memory/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md: the raw running record, only ever appended to.
- memory/reference/<topic>.md (README.md is the index): curated topic documents that get rewritten; their content is
  the most accurate current version, and where it conflicts with the older running record, reference/ wins.
